svg.text: How a double gets a tag without losing a bit
Rotating left by 4 moves the top 4 bits to the bottom, and 2 of them become the tag.
+ BIAS (0x6810_0000_0000_0000), so those two bits read 10 for every inline double
The top 4 bits end up at the bottom
bits 3..0 are the old 63..60, and 1..0 are now the tag
Nothing is destroyed, so the mapping is exact and decoding is a rotate and a subtract.
The doubles whose exponent bits do not land on 10 are the only ones that get boxed:
magnitudes from 3.4e38 to 5.3e269, and from 1.9e-270 to 2.9e-39. Everything else
stays inline: the normal float32 range, +-0.0, double subnormals, +-inf and every NaN.
